instruction: School Space Summary Model. Start from a blank OpenStudio model. There are no init_file inputs and no local reference images for this task. Use OpenStudio GUI operations, measures, scripts, or API calls to create a one-story school support model and save the required outputs as /home/user/Desktop/result.osm and /home/user/Desktop/result.csv. Every required output must be a valid, non-empty file at the stated Desktop path. The final model requirements are: - the result.osm model contains exactly 1 OS:Building, 1 OS:BuildingStory, 6 OS:Space objects, and 6 OS:ThermalZone objects; - the OS:Space names are exactly Classroom-1, Classroom-2, Corridor, Restroom, Office, and Storage; - every OS:Space references the OS:BuildingStory, references an OS:ThermalZone, has Part of Total Floor Area set to Yes, and has floor area greater than 0.05 m2; - the result.osm model contains at least one OS:DefaultConstructionSet and the single OS:Building references a default construction set; - the model has exactly 42 OS:Surface objects: 6 Floor surfaces, 6 RoofCeiling surfaces, and 30 Wall surfaces; - the surface Outside Boundary Condition counts are exactly 6 Ground, 20 Outdoors, and 16 Surface; - the model contains exactly 0 OS:SubSurface objects; - the surface geometry bounding box has X span 22.00 m, Y span 10.00 m, and Z span 3.40 m, each with tolerance +/-0.05 m; - the sum of floor surface areas is 176.00 m2 with tolerance +/-0.50 m2; - the sum of exterior wall gross areas is 217.60 m2 with tolerance +/-0.50 m2 Prepare the required supporting files so that the result.csv report has exactly the header row space_name,floor_area_m2,space_type_name,thermal_zone_name and 6 data rows in this order: Classroom-1, Classroom-2, Corridor, Office, Restroom, Storage; each result.csv floor_area_m2 value matches the evaluator-computed floor area for that space with tolerance +/-0.20 m2, and each CSV space_type_name and thermal_zone_name matches the corresponding OpenStudio object name. Details not named here may vary, including object handles, GUIDs, incidental metadata, construction names, material definitions, and serializer ordering, as long as the required OpenStudio objects, geometry, relationships, and output data are correct. [Software] Launch the OpenStudio GUI with `OpenStudioApp` from a terminal (PATH or full path to the binary).
